   98.5  Flap or pedicle graft
   NOTE:  1. Functional areas includes the following anatomical areas:
             Head, neck, axillae, elbow, wrist, hand, groin, perineum,
             hip, knee, ankle, foot and includes coverage of exposed
             vital structures (bone, tendon, major vessel, nerve)
          2. Flaps (HSCs 98.53,98.5A,98.51A,98.51B) for functional areas
             are designated by FNCAR modifier, add 50% to total benefit.
          3. Flap size 5-10 cms or double Z-plasty designated by 2ZPL
             modifier, add 25% to benefit.
          4. Flap size greater than 10 cms or triple Z-plasty designated
             by 3ZPL modifier, add 50% to benefit.
          5. Composite tissue resection (includes bone) designated by
             CMPRSC modifier, add 25% to benefit.
          6. Only one modifier (CMPRSC, FNCAR, 2ZPL, 3ZPL) may be claimed
             per flap.

   Standard Out-Patient Visit, including select discrete high cost
   diagnostic imaging procedures. Excludes specific services identified
   within other service codes.
   NOTE:  (a)  An out-patient is an individual who has been officially
               accepted by a hospital and receives one or more
               health services without being admitted as an in-patient; and
               whose person identifiable data is recorded in the
               registration or information system of the organization and
               to whom a unique identifier is assigned to record and track
               services.

          (b)  Select discrete high cost diagnostic imaging procedures
               include the following:
                  1. Nuclear Medicine - diagnostic images and treatment
                     procedures using radiopharmaceuticals. Includes single
                     photon emission computed tomography (SPECT).
                     Excludes nuclear medicine scans superimposed on images
                     from modalities such as CT or MRI
                     (e.g. SPECT/CT, PET/CT) which have their own service
                     codes.
                  2. Fluoroscopy - an imaging technique to obtain real-time
                     moving images of a patient through a fluoroscope,
                     developed from the capture of external ionizing
                     radiation on a fluorescent screen.
                  3. Ultrasound - the production of a visual record of body
                     tissues by means of high frequency sound waves.
                  4. Interventional/Angiography Studies - the use of
                     radiant energy from x-ray equipment during
                     interventional and angiography studies.
                     These radiography techniques use minimally invasive
                     methods and imaging guidance to perform studies that
                     replace conventional surgery such as diagnostic
                     arteriography, renal and peripheral vasular
                     interventions, biliary, venous access procedures and
                     embolization.

               condition.

          (b)  The charge in this section will include the cost of supplies
               normally used in any procedure but do not include supplies for
